plain_english: Arjuna said: O Keśava, I wish to know nature and person, field and field-knower, knowledge and the knowable. Scripture somewhere says the field-knower is to be worshipped; is he the Self or the Lord, or some third other? Thus, amid this question and doubt, the holy Lord instructs.
sanskrit_cite: atha trayodaśo'dhyāyaḥ   arjuna uvāca   prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva kṣetraṃ kṣetrajñameva ca | etadveditumicchāmi jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ ca keśava | kvacicchrutau kṣetrajña upāsyaḥ-iti śrūyate | sa ca kimātmā  uteśvaraḥ atha tṛtīyaḥ kaścidanya eva ? iti praśnāśaṅkāyāṃ  śrībhagavānādiśati-

plain_english: The blessed Lord said: This body, O son of Kunti, is called the field; he who knows this, the knowers of that call the field-knower.
sanskrit_cite: śrībhagavānuvāca   idaṃ śarīraṃ kaunteya kṣetramityabhidhīyate | etadyo veda taṃ  prāhuḥ kṣetrajña iti tadvidaḥ

plain_english: Know Me as the knower of the field in all fields, O Bhārata; the knowing of field and knower of the field — that is deemed knowing by Me. The body of transmigrators is the field, wherein karma-seeds sprout; hence their self, stained by adventitious impurity, is called the knower; for the awakened it is the same field distinctly.
sanskrit_cite: kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi sarvakṣetreṣu bhārata | kṣetrakṣetrajñayorjñānaṃ yattajjñānaṃ mataṃ mama | saṃsāriṇāṃ śarīraṃ kṣetraṃ yatra karmabījaprarohaḥ | ata eva  teṣāmātmā āgantukakāluṣyarūṣitaḥ kṣetrajña ucyate | prabuddhānāṃ tadeva kṣetram | anvarthabhedastu tadyathā-kṣiṇoti  karmabandhamupabhogena trāyate janmamaraṇabhayāditi | tāṃśca prati  paramātmā vāsudevaḥ kṣetrajñaḥ etatkṣetraṃ yo veda-vedayati  ityantarbhāvitaṇyartho vidiḥ | tena yatprasādādacetanamidaṃ  cetanībhāvamāyāti sa eva kṣetrajño nānyaḥ kaścit | viśeṣastu  parimitavyāptikaṃ rūpamālambya ātmeti bhaṇyate  aparicchinnasarvakṣetravyāptyā paramātmā bhagavānvāsudevaḥ  mameti karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī-ahamanena jñānena jñeya ityarthaḥ

plain_english: Hear from me in brief what that field is, of what kind, with what modifications, from what, what it is, who its knower is, and of what nature.
sanskrit_cite: tatkṣetraṃ yacca yādṛkca yadvikāri yataśca yat | sa ca yo  yatsvabhāvaśca tatsamāsena me śṛṇu

plain_english: Although sages and Vedas have taught this in many ways, through various meters and reasoned Brahmasūtra words, distinguishing transformation and the transformed by a common answer without distinction, I will explain it in summary.
sanskrit_cite: ṛṣibhirbahudhā gītaṃ chandobhirvividhaiḥ pṛthak | brahmasūtrapadaiścaiva hetumadbhirviniścitam | yena vikāraṃ gacchati yadvikāri | samāsena-ityavibhāgenaivaitānpraśnān sādhāraṇottareṇa  paricchinatti | yadyapi ca ṛṣibhirbahudhā vedaiścoktametat tathāpi  samāsenāhaṃ vyācakṣa iti

plain_english: The great elements, ego, intellect, and unmanifest; the senses are eleven, and five are sense-objects; the unmanifest is nature; senses with mind are eleven; sense-objects are forms and the rest, five.
sanskrit_cite: mahābhūtānyahaṅkāro buddhiravyaktameva ca | indriyāṇi daśaikaṃ  ca pañca cendriyagocarāḥ | avyaktaṃ-prakṛtiḥ | indriyāṇi-manasā sahaikādaśa | indriyagocarāḥ-rūpādayaḥ pañca

plain_english: Desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, aggregate consciousness, and steadiness are this field in brief; consciousness-seeing power is the person. Thus the field is explained, and the field-knower; now knowledge is declared.
sanskrit_cite: icchā dveṣaḥ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ saṅghātaścetanā dhṛtiḥ | etatkṣetraṃ samāsena savikāramudāhṛtam | cetanā-dṛkśaktiḥ puruṣaḥ | dhṛtiriti ante kila sarvasya-ā  brahmaṇaḥ krimiparyantasya prārabdhe niṣpanne vā kārye  kāmakrodhādiṣu ca iyataiva mama paryāptaṃ kimanyena  īdṛśaścāhaṃ nityameva bhūyāsam-iti prāṇasaṃghāriṇī  dhṛtirāśvāsanātmikā pararahasyaśāsaneṣu rāgaśabdavācyā  jāyate | evaṃ kṣetraṃ vyākhyātaṃ kṣetrajñaśca | idānīṃ  jñānamucyate-

plain_english: Humility, nonpretense, nonviolence, patience, straightness, service to the teacher, purity, steadiness, and self-restraint.
sanskrit_cite: amānitvamadambhitvamahiṃsā kṣāntirārjavam | ācāryopāsanaṃ  śaucaṃ sthairyamātmavinigrahaḥ

plain_english: Dispassion and non-egoism in sense objects, and seeing the faults of birth, death, age, disease, and suffering.
sanskrit_cite: indriyārtheṣu vairāgyamanahaṅkāra eva ca | janmamṛtyujarāvyādhiduḥkhadoṣānudarśanam

plain_english: Non-attachment and non-clinging in son, wife, house, and so on, and always equal-mindedness in desired and undesired occurrences.
sanskrit_cite: asaktiranabhiṣvaṅgaḥ putradāragṛhādiṣu | nityaṃ ca  samacittatvamiṣṭāniṣṭopapattiṣu

plain_english: Unwavering devotion to me by non-other yoga, residence in a secluded place, and dislike for crowds.
sanskrit_cite: mayi cānanyayogena bhaktiravyabhicāriṇī | viviktadeśasevitvamaratirjanasaṃsadi

plain_english: Steadfastness in self-knowledge and seeing the purpose of truth-knowledge are this knowledge; what is otherwise is ignorance. Certainty that nothing apart from the supreme self exists is yoga; by that certainty devotion to me does not deviate. Thus everything is to be connected; the opposite of this is ignorance, and pride and the rest. By this knowledge what is to be known is declared.
sanskrit_cite: adhyātmajñānaniṣṭhatvaṃ tattvajñānārthadarśanam | etajjñānamiti proktamajñānaṃ yadato'nyathā | ananyayogeneti-paramātmano maheśvarādanyadaparaṃ na  kiṃcidasti-ityananyarūpo yo niścayaḥ sa eva yogaḥ-tena niścayena  mayi bhaktiḥ | ata eva sā na  kadācidvyabhicarati-vyabhicārahetutvābhimatānāṃ  kāmanānāmabhāvāt tāsāmapi vā cittavṛttyantararūpāṇāṃ  tadekamayatvāt | evaṃ sarvatrānusaṃdheyam etadviparītamajñānam  tathā mānitvādīni | etena jñānena yajjñeyaṃ taducyate-

plain_english: I shall declare that which is to be known, by knowing which one eats immortality: the beginningless supreme Brahman, called neither existent nor nonexistent.
sanskrit_cite: jñeyaṃ yattatpravakṣyāmi yajjñātvā'mṛtamaśnute | anādimatparaṃ brahma na sattannāsaducyate

plain_english: Everywhere are its hands and feet; everywhere its eyes, heads, and mouths; everywhere hearing in the world; having pervaded all, it stands.
sanskrit_cite: sarvataḥ pāṇipādaṃ tatsarvato'kṣiśiromukham | sarvataḥ  śrutimalloke sarvamāvṛttya tiṣṭhati

plain_english: It is the reflection of all sense qualities, yet devoid of all senses; unattached, bearer of all, without strands, and enjoyer of strands.
sanskrit_cite: sarvendriyaguṇābhāsaṃ sarvendriyavivarjitam | asaktaṃ  sarvabhṛccaiva nirguṇaṃ guṇabhoktṛ ca

plain_english: It is outside and inside beings, moving and unmoving; because of subtlety it is unknowable, far and near.
sanskrit_cite: bahirantaśca bhūtānāmacaraṃ carameva ca | sūkṣmatvāttadavijñeyaṃ dūrasthaṃ cāntike ca tat

plain_english: Undivided in beings, yet as if divided, it stands; bearer of beings, that to-be-known, devouring and ruling.
sanskrit_cite: avibhaktaṃ ca bhūteṣu vibhaktamiva ca sthitam | bhūtabhartṛ ca  tajjñeyaṃ grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca

plain_english: That light beyond darkness is called supreme; knowing and known, reachable by knowing, it abides in the heart of all; beginningless supreme Brahman, by qualifiers beginning with Brahman indicating and supporting Brahman's nature, non-different from knowledge stated by all doctrines, is declared. These qualifiers were already explained; what fruitless repetition?
sanskrit_cite: jyotiṣāmapi tajjyotistamasaḥ paramucyate | jñānajñeyaṃ  jñānagamyaṃ hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam | anādimatparaṃ  brahma-ityādibhirviśeṣaṇairbrahmasvarūpākṣepānugrāhakaṃ  sarvapravādābhihitavijñānāpṛthagbhāvaṃ kathayati | etāni ca  viśeṣaṇāṇi pūrvameva vyākhyātānīti kiṃ niṣphalayā  punaruktyā

plain_english: This field, knowing, and the known are stated in brief; one who knows this triad is the Lord's devotee and attains the Lord's state.
sanskrit_cite: etatkṣetraṃ tathā jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ coktaṃ samāsataḥ | madbhakta  etadvijñāya madbhāvāyopapadyate | etatkṣetrajñānajñeyātmakaṃ trayaṃ yo vetti sa eva madbhaktaḥ | sa ca madbhāvameti | etallakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā parīkṣā kriyate-

plain_english: Know nature and person as beginningless, along with modifications and strands born from nature.
sanskrit_cite: prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva viddhyanādī ubhāvapi | vikārāṁśca  guṇāṁścaiva viddhi prakṛtisambhavān | prakṛtirapyanādiḥ-kāraṇāntarābhāvāt | vikārāḥ-paṭādayaḥ

plain_english: Nature is called the cause in action and instrumentality, while person is called the cause in enjoying pleasures and pains.
sanskrit_cite: kāryakaraṇakartṛtve hetuḥ prakṛtirucyate | puruṣaḥ  sukhaduḥkhānāṃ bhoktṛtve heturucyate | prakṛtiriti kāryakāraṇabhāve hetuḥ | puruṣastu  prādhānyādbhoktā

plain_english: The person standing in nature enjoys strands born from nature; attachment to strands causes births, and nature and person function in mutual dependence.
sanskrit_cite: puruṣaḥ prakṛtistho hi bhuṅkte prakṛtijānguṇān | kāraṇaṃ  guṇasaṅgo'sya sadasadyonijanmasu | prakṛtipuruṣayoḥ paṅgvandhavatkilānyonyāpekṣā vṛttiḥ

plain_english: The supreme person in the body is witness, consenter, supporter, enjoyer, and great lord; nature, its fourteen-fold modification, and creation are beginningless and eternal.
sanskrit_cite: upadraṣṭānumantā ca bhartā bhoktā maheśvaraḥ | paramātmeti  cāpyukto dehe'sminpuruṣaḥ paraḥ | ata evāsya śāstrakṛdbhirnānākārairnāmabhirabhidhīyate  rūpam-upadraṣṭā-ityādibhiḥ | ayamatra tātparyārthaḥ | prakṛtiḥ tadvikāraścaturdaśavidhaḥ sargaḥ tathā  puruṣaḥ-etatsarvamanādi nityaṃ ca brahmatattvācchuritatve sati  tadananyatvāt | tathā cāha-

plain_english: One who knows person, nature, strands, and modifications is not born again; even while acting, such a yogi is liberated.
sanskrit_cite: ya evaṃ vetti puruṣaṃ prakṛtiṃ ca guṇaiḥ saha | sarvathā  vartamāno'pi na sa bhūyo'bhijāyate | evam-anena sarvābhedarūpeṇa brahmadarśanena yo yogī prakṛtiṃ  puruṣaṃ guṇāṃśca tadvikārān jānāti | sarveṇa prakāreṇa  yathātathā vartamāno'pi sa mukta evetyarthaḥ

plain_english: Some see the self by meditation, others by sāṃkhya, yoga, or karma-yoga.
sanskrit_cite: dhyānenā''tmani paśyanti kecidātmānamātmanā | anye sāṅkhyena  yogena karmayogena cāpare

plain_english: Others, not knowing thus, hear from others and worship; they too cross death.
sanskrit_cite: anye tvevamajānantaḥ śrutvānyebhya upāsate | te'pi cātitarantyeva  mṛtyuṃ śrutiparāyaṇāḥ | īdṛśaṃ ca jñānaṃ pradhānaṃ kaiścidātmatayā upāsyate | anyaiḥ prāguktena sāṃkhyanayena | aparaiḥ karmaṇā | itarairapi  svayamīdṛśaṃ jñānamajānadbhirapi  śravaṇapravaṇairyathāśrutamevopāsyate | te'pi mṛtyuṃsaṃsāraṃ  taranti | yenakenacidupāyena bhagavattattvamupasyamānamuttārayati | ataḥ sarvathaivamāsītetyuktam

plain_english: Whatever exists, moving or still, arises from field-knower union; nothing exists beyond the knower.
sanskrit_cite: yāvatkiñcitsambhavati sattvaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam | kṣetrakṣetrajñasaṃyogāttadviddhi bharatarṣabha | yatkiṃcit caramacaraṃ ca tatsarvaṃ kṣetrajñātireki na  saṃbhavatīti

plain_english: He who sees the supreme lord standing equally in all beings, perishing with the perishing, truly sees.
sanskrit_cite: samaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhantaṃ parameśvaram | vinaśyatsvavinaśyantaṃ yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati

plain_english: Seeing the lord equally everywhere, one does not harm oneself and reaches the supreme goal.
sanskrit_cite: ata eva   samaṃ paśyan hi sarvatra samavasthitamīśvaram | na  hinastyātmanātmānaṃ tato yāti parāṃ gatim | sarvatraiva samabuddhiryogī ātmānaṃ na hinasti-dustare  saṃsārārṇave na pātayati

plain_english: Seeing actions done by nature and the self as non-doer, one truly sees.
sanskrit_cite: prakṛtyaiva hi karmāṇi kriyamāṇāni sarvaśaḥ | yaḥ paśyati  tathātmānamakartāraṃ sa paśyati | yasya hi īdṛśī sthiratarā buddhirbhavati-prakṛtirevedaṃ karoti  nāhaṃ kiṃcit sa sarvaṃ kuvāṇo'pi na karoti | evamakartṛtvam

plain_english: When one sees distinct beings as unified, then brahman is attained.
sanskrit_cite: yadi vā   yadā bhūtapṛthagbhāvamekasthamunapaśyati | tata eva ca vistāraṃ  brahma sampadyate tadā

plain_english: The beginningless, qualityless supreme self, though in the body, neither acts nor is stained.
sanskrit_cite: anāditvānnirguṇatvātparamātmā'yamavyayaḥ | śarīrastho'pi  kaunteya na karoti na lipyate

plain_english: As space remains unstained, so the self remains unstained even in the body.
sanskrit_cite: yathā sarvagataṃ saukṣmyādākāśaṃ nopalipyate | sarvatrāvasthito  dehe tathātmā nopalipyate | vistīrṇatvena sarvavyāptyā yadā bhūtānāṃ  pṛthaktāṃ-bhinnatām ātmanyeva paśyati ātmana eva coditāṃ tāṃ  manyate | tadāpi sarvakartṛtvānna lepabhāk | yato'sau paramātmaiva  śarīrastho'pi na lipyate-ākāśavat

plain_english: As the sun illuminates the world, the supreme self illuminates all fields.
sanskrit_cite: yathā prakāśayatyekaḥ kṛtsnaṃ lokamimaṃ raviḥ | kṣetraṃ  kṣetrī tathā kṛtsnaṃ prakāśayati bhārata | nanu ekaḥ paramātmā kathamanekāni kṣetrāṇi vyāpnoti  ?-ityāśaṅkā prasiddhena raviṇā dṛṣṭāntenāpākṛtā | kṛtsnaṃ kṣetraṃ-carācarāṇi kṣetrāṇītyarthaḥ

plain_english: Those who know the difference between field and knower attain supreme Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: kṣetrakṣetrajñayorevamantaraṃ jñānacakṣuṣā | bhūtaprakṛtimokṣaṃ ca ye viduryānti te param | evamadhyāyena yaduktaṃ jñeyaṃ jñānaṃ  kṣetrakṣetrajñayorantaraṃ bhūtaprakṛteśca  svalpātpariṇāmadharmatvānmocanaṃ tat ye jñānalakṣaṇena  sarvatrāpratihatenālaukikena cakṣuṣā paśyanti te vāsudevatāṃ  prāpya labhanta eva paramaṃ śivamiti śivam

plain_english: Here is the summary verse: confused minds see person and nature as distinct, while the complete see the world as pure self.
sanskrit_cite: atra saṃgrahaślokaḥ   pumānprakṛtirityeṣa bhedaḥ saṃmūḍhacetasām | paripūrṇāstu  manyante nirmalātmamayaṃ jagat | iti śrīmahāmaheśvarācāryavaryarājānakābhinavaguptapādaviracite  śrīmadbhagavadgītārthasaṃgrahe trayodaśo'dhyāyaḥ
